name: Sins of the Tongue

counsel.text: This commandment binds the tongue to its good behaviour. God has set two natural fences to keep in the tongue, the teeth and lips; and this commandment is a third fence set about it, that it should not break forth into evil.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Ten Commandments, the ninth commandment

counsel.text: Rise mightily against the first actings of thy distemper, its first conceptions; suffer it not to get the least ground. Do not say, "Thus far it shall go, and no farther." If it have allowance for one step, it will take another. It is impossible to fix bounds to sin. It is like water in a channel, -- if it once break out, it will have its course.
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 11

counsel.text: The slanderer wounds three at once: he wounds him that is slandered; he wounds him to whom he reports the slander, by causing uncharitable thoughts to arise up in his mind against the party slandered; and he wounds his own soul, by reporting of another what is false.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Ten Commandments, the ninth commandment

counsel.text: Love is a well-wisher, and it is rare to speak ill of him we wish well to. Love is that which cements Christians together; it is the healer of division, and the hinderer of slander.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Ten Commandments, the ninth commandment

counsel.text: I say, then, by faith, be much in the consideration of that supply and the fulness of it that is in Jesus Christ, and how he can at any time give thee strength and deliverance.
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 14

counsel.text: A man may wrong another as well by silence as by slander, when he knows him to be wrongfully accused, yet does not speak in his behalf. If others cast false aspersions on any, we should wipe them off.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Ten Commandments, the ninth commandment

counsel.text: As we have a portion in the communion of saints, so we should labour to have humility to take good, and wisdom and love to do good. A Christian should have feeding lips and a healing tongue. The leaves, the very words, of the tree of righteousness have a curing virtue in them.
counsel.author: Richard Sibbes
counsel.source: The Soul's Conflict with Itself, ch. 14

counsel.text: Men think themselves freed from murder if they kill none, or if they shed no blood, whereas they cut others to the heart with bitter words. It is good to extend the commandment to awake the conscience the more, and breed humility, when men see there is a murdering of the tongue.
counsel.author: Richard Sibbes
counsel.source: The Soul's Conflict with Itself, ch. 2

counsel.text: Let men take heed of taking up Satan's office, in depraving the good actions of others, as he did Job's, 'doth he serve God for nought?' Job 1. 9, or slandering their persons, judging of them according to the wickedness that is in their own hearts.
counsel.author: Richard Sibbes

counsel.text: The Spirit of God is a Spirit of peace and love, and therefore delights not to breathe in a troubled air. The ready way to send him going is to brawl and chide.
counsel.author: William Gurnall

counsel.text: A sincere heart is like a clear stream in a brook; you may see to the bottom of his plots in his words, and take the measure of his heart by his tongue.
counsel.author: William Gurnall

counsel.text: The language of a murmuring, a muttering soul is this, Surely God might have done this sooner, and that wiser, and the other thing better, &c. As the river Nilus bringeth forth many crocodiles, and the scorpion many serpents at one birth, so murmuring is a sin that breeds and brings forth many sins at once. Murmuring is like the monster hydra; cut off one head, and many will rise up in its room.
counsel.author: Thomas Brooks
counsel.source: The Mute Christian Under the Smarting Rod

prayers.title: A prayer of confession
prayers.opening: Holy Father, every word I speak is known to you, and your own words are pure, like silver refined seven times; I bless you that I may come to you through Jesus Christ, the Word made flesh.
prayers.text: I confess that I have sinned with my tongue. I have gossiped and slandered, spoken harshly, boasted, complained, mocked, and flattered. I have torn down what you call me to build up. With the same tongue I have blessed you and cursed people made in your likeness. My tongue has been a fire, and it has shown the evil in my heart, for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks. The problem is not only my words but the pride, envy, and anger they come from. Forgive me, Lord. Christ never spoke a sinful word; when he was reviled, he did not revile in return, and gracious words came from his lips. For his sake pardon me, and give me grace to seek forgiveness from those I have wounded. Holy Spirit, put this sin to death and make my heart clean, so that my speech will be gracious.
prayers.closing: I thank you that you have put a new song in my mouth, a song of praise to our God. Let the words of my mouth be acceptable in your sight, O Lord, my rock and my redeemer. Amen.

prayers.title: Before I speak
prayers.opening: O Lord, you hear every word before it is on my tongue, and your words are life.
prayers.text: Lord, set a guard over my mouth and keep watch over the door of my lips. I am about to say something I should not. Stop me. Make me quick to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger. Let no corrupting talk come out of my mouth, but only what is good for building up, so that it may give grace to those who hear. If I must speak a hard truth, let me speak it in love, or wait until I can. Lord Jesus, give me your words.
prayers.closing: Blessed be your name for ever. Amen.

prayers.title: For gracious speech
prayers.opening: Father, I praise you, the God who speaks, whose words are sweeter than honey to my mouth.
prayers.text: Father, let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable in your sight, O Lord, my rock and my redeemer. Make my speech always gracious, seasoned with salt. Teach me to encourage, to give thanks, to speak well of others when they are absent, and to keep confidences. Give me courage to speak of Christ, and wisdom to be silent when silence is better. Use my tongue to bless my family, my church, and my neighbors.
prayers.closing: Through Jesus Christ, whose lips were full of grace, to whom be praise for ever. Amen.

prayers.title: Confessing the sins of our tongue
prayers.opening: Thou art he that hearest prayer, and therefore unto thee shall all flesh come.
prayers.text: In the multitude of our words there wanteth not sin, nor can a man full of talk be justified. While the lips of the righteous feed many, our lips have poured out foolishness, and spoken frowardness. Much corrupt communication hath proceeded out of our mouths; that foolish talking and jesting which is not convenient; and little of that which is good, and to the use of edifying, and which might minister grace unto the hearers. If for every idle word that men speak they must give an account, and by our words we must be justified, and by our words we must be condemned, woe unto us; for we are undone! for we are of unclean lips, and dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips.
prayers.closing: Let the words of our mouths, and the meditations of our hearts, be acceptable in thy sight, O Lord, our strength and our Redeemer. To God, only wise, be glory through Jesus Christ for ever. Amen.
prayers.author: Matthew Henry
prayers.source: arranged from A Method for Prayer, chs. 1, 2 and 7

prayers.title: To govern our tongues well
prayers.opening: Thou hast appointed us a great High Priest, in whose name we may come boldly to the throne of grace, that we may find mercy and grace to help in time of need.
prayers.text: Lord, enable us to take heed to our ways, that we offend not with our tongue, and to keep our mouth as it were with a bridle, that it may not be hasty to utter any thing. Set a watch, O Lord, before our mouth, keep the door of our lips, that we may not offend in word. Let our speech be always with grace, seasoned with salt, and enable us always out of the good treasure of our heart to bring forth good things. Let our mouth speak wisdom, and our tongue talk of judgment; and let not thy words depart out of our mouth, nor out of the mouth of our seed, or our seed's seed, from henceforth and for ever. Enable us always to open our mouth with wisdom, and let the law of kindness be in our tongue: give us to know what is acceptable, that our tongue may be as choice silver, and our lips may feed many.
prayers.closing: Let the words of our mouths, and the meditations of our hearts, be acceptable in thy sight, O Lord, our strength and our Redeemer. To God, only wise, be glory through Jesus Christ for ever. Amen.
prayers.author: Matthew Henry
prayers.source: arranged from A Method for Prayer, chs. 1, 3 and 7

examinationQuestions: When your words went wrong today, what was in your heart just before you spoke: anger, envy, pride, or the wish to be liked?
Whom did your words make smaller today, and what does that show about how you are seeing them, and how you are seeing God?
Did you say anything about someone today that you would not have said if they were in the room?
Is there anyone you need to go to and ask forgiveness for something you said, or a false report you need to set right?
When you complain about others, are you quietly complaining against God, who put them in your life?
Did your talk today give thanks and build others up, or was it mostly about yourself?
fleeActions: Close your mouth and step away from the conversation. Say nothing more until you have prayed.
If you are typing a message, delete it now. Do not send anything about this until tomorrow.
If others are gossiping, change the subject, or say plainly that you would rather not talk about someone who is not here.
Go to the person you spoke against, or the one you spoke to, and make it right today.
Pray for the person you were about to criticize by name, and thank God for one good thing in them.
Open your Bible to James 3 and read it slowly before you say another word.

afterFallReadings.text: Christ, by his intercession, calls for acquittance. Lord, he says, let the sinner be absolved from guilt; and in this sense he is called an advocate. 1 John 2:2. He requires that the sinner be set free in the court.
afterFallReadings.author: Thomas Watson
afterFallReadings.source: A Body of Divinity, Christ's priestly office
